subject: Taxes
title: Debt vs. Equity: The Tax Bias
description: A 60-second lesson on Debt vs. Equity: The Tax Bias.

hook.text: Interest on debt is tax-deductible. Dividends are not. This single rule shapes how every corporation finances itself.

buildup.text: A company borrowing $1 billion at 5% interest can deduct $50 million annually.

discovery.text: This creates a massive incentive to use debt over equity.

twist.text: Private equity firms exploit this ruthlessly. They buy companies, load them with debt, deduct the interest.

climax.text: The debt-equity tax bias distorts the entire economy.

punchline.text: Borrow and deduct. The tax code's bias toward debt shapes every deal.

quiz.question: Why do companies prefer debt over equity financing?
options: Interest payments are tax-deductible but dividends are not
Equity is illegal for large companies
